name: two-tip
title: Two tip
description: Zenith's starter example auto (examples/starter collect-and-score), tuned to BioHORS: shoot the four preloads from the south, which tips the hive (3 nectar staged in the up cell); go round the west of the hive to flower1 and score its four in the north cell; sweep the RED garden line west and score its four north for the second tip. The flower bar goes down only to collect from the flower.

steps.notes: A straight line north to the scoring spot south of the hive, facing its up cell.

steps.name: score
steps.notes: Volley 1: the four preloads into the south cell; the third tips it (3 nectar staged there, season tip table) and the fourth goes in as it starts to swing.

control.provenance: SET BY HAND: the starter example's first control point moved 6 in west and 4 in south, tuned to BioHORS: the 22 in robot clears the hive frame's west bar as it turns

PLACEHOLDER: starter example, a curve control point that takes the robot around the west of the hive frame, clear of its west bar and legs, so the whole footprint stays on RED's side of the centre line

PLACEHOLDER: starter example, a curve control point that takes the robot around the west of the hive frame, clear of its west bar and legs, so the whole footprint stays on RED's side of the centre line

steps.notes: After the tip the up cell faces north, and a launch only scores from the up cell's own quarter of the field, so the robot goes to the other side of the hive. It goes around the west of the hive frame, not under it: the frame's west legs keep an 18 in robot's centre east of about x = -9, and its footprint is 18 in wide, so under the hive it would cross the centre line into BLUE's side (G402). It keeps facing north while it leaves the scoring spot, turns to drive nose-first once its footprint is clear of the centre line, and turns back to face north for the flower. Pedro reads a piece's end as a fraction of the path's length and hands a tangent piece its own 0..1 t, so the starter's tangent spans are written as linear pieces between the curve's true direction every tenth of the path (tools/zenith_headings.py); each piece starts on the heading the last one ended on, so the robot never spins on the spot.

steps.name: intakeOn
steps.notes: Starts the intake before the flower. (Pedro 3.0.2 cannot run Zenith's mid-path markers, so the starter's t = 0 marker is a command first.)

steps.name: flowerBarDown
steps.notes: Puts the flower bar down to reach into flower1's opening.

Drives slowly all the way in to flower1 with the intake running and the bar down (0.2, SET BY HAND, the team: slower, and in closer). It no longer stops early when the hopper reads full: it always reaches the pickup, and expect tells the ledger it takes the flower's four pollen. Heading held square to the wall (a tangent heading turns a small sideways offset into a yaw that swings the mouth off the opening).
Gives the intake up to 1.5 s more (SET BY HAND, the team: longer at the flower). A wait until ends as soon as its condition is true, and timeoutS stops it waiting forever.
SET BY HAND (the team): holds the intake running and the bar down 0.5 s more after the hopper reads full, so a last pollen still in the mouth comes in before the bar lifts.

steps.name: flowerBarStow
steps.notes: Folds the flower bar up before backing off.

steps.name: score
steps.notes: Volley 2: four flower pollen into the north cell (up after tip 1).

steps.notes: The starter's curve back south round the west of the hive, tuned to BioHORS (CAD footprint: bar tip 14.2 in ahead of the drive centre, back 7.8 in behind, 17.84 in wide); ending heading west above the garden lane instead of turning to west on it. Pedro reads a piece's end as a fraction of the path's length and hands a tangent piece its own 0..1 t, so the starter's tangent spans are written as linear pieces between the curve's true direction every tenth of the path (tools/zenith_headings.py); each piece starts on the heading the last one ended on, so the robot never spins on the spot.
Slides down onto the garden lane still facing west, slowly so it stops on time: near the south wall the 22 in robot must stay square to it.

steps.name: intakeOn
steps.notes: Starts the intake before the sweep. (Pedro 3.0.2 cannot run Zenith's mid-path markers, so the starter's t = 0 marker is a command first.)

The starter's sweep west along the RED garden line, intake toward the red alliance wall, taking the pollen in a line. It always runs to its end: cut short when full, the robot rolls on into the west wall. Slower than the starter's 0.3 (0.2, SET BY HAND, the team's call): every pollen in the row has time to go in.
Up to 0.8 s more for the last pollen.
Up off the lane still facing west (square to the south wall), to where it can turn.

It does the turn west of x = -13, and the last stretch is a straight drive south, so its footprint stays on RED's side of the centre line (G402). A deadline group ends when its deadline member, the drive, ends. The sequence beside it keeps the intake on for half a second while the robot leaves the garden, then stops it and spins the launcher up on the way back.

steps.notes: Four more pollen into the north cell, which now holds 8, so the hive tips a second time.
